description: Opt-in preset for products on the @tanksterai UI packages (@tanksterai/tokens, @tanksterai/css, @tanksterai/react), published to GitHub Packages. Add it after the language preset: "extends": ["github>TanksterAI/.github:node", "github>TanksterAI/.github:tanksterai-ui"]. Requires the TANKSTERAI_PACKAGES_TOKEN credential in the Mend developer portal: a repository that extends this preset without it stops with a Renovate config error. It is not part of default.json or node.json for exactly that reason.

hostRules.description: Read-only access to the org's GitHub Packages npm registry. The secret is a classic token with read:packages only, stored as an organisation credential at developer.mend.io and never in a repository.

packageRules.description: Look the @tanksterai scope up on GitHub Packages, not npmjs.org. The npmrc line above already does this; stating it here as well keeps lookups right if a repository's own .npmrc, .yarnrc or pnpm-workspace.yaml maps the scope elsewhere.

The UI packages are ours and are released together, so they arrive together and at once: one 'tanksterai-ui' pull request, outside the monthly window, with no release-age wait. The release-age wait is off because a regression in our own package is ours to find, and timestamp-optional means a missing publish time is never a reason to hold one back. Always human-reviewed: automerge is set off explicitly because default.json automerges devDependencies, and these are often devDependencies.
A major of the UI packages is a migration across the product. No pull request until it is ticked on the Dependency Dashboard.

@tanksterai/design-tokens was replaced by @tanksterai/tokens. Renovate never updates it, so a repository still on it gets no pull requests for it and has to migrate to @tanksterai/tokens by hand. Renovate cannot stop someone adding it back to a package.json; this only keeps it out of update pull requests.
